comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Fixed. The cause is that a Muster pane does not scroll: its daemon holds the history and answers a
scroll by re-encoding the new screen as cell writes, so a ten-row scroll arrives as absolute cursor
moves and one glyph per changed cell. libghostty pins a selection to rows of its own buffer, and
that buffer never moved - the text under the highlight was simply rewritten. Measured and written
up as section 12 of `docs/observations/libghostty-9f9b8d1d.md`.

So a selection is remembered in the pane's own coordinates - a column and a row counted up from the
bottom of its history, the same unit a search's landing uses - and asked for again wherever the
pane has travelled to. The seam gains one read for where a pane is looking, coalesced like a
divider drag and only sent while something is selected.

Worth knowing about what it does not cover:

- A double or triple click selects a word or a line, and libghostty exports no way to read back
  which cells that covered. Those selections are left alone rather than pinned to the one cell
  that was clicked, so they still drift on a scroll. Carded as a_2Jrhh1dkA.
- Landing on a find scrolls the pane without the window asking for it, so a selection made and then
  searched past is not re-placed until the next scroll. Carded as a_2JrhrSBOx.
- Whether libghostty then paints the right cells is not something the suite can judge: a real
  surface needs a GPU and a window. What is tested is the decision - which cells were asked for,
  and when the answer is that there is nothing to draw - through the same fake surface the rest of
  the view's decisions use. That is the same footing `highlight` and `setFontSizeOffset` have
  stood on since they were written.
